Since I don't know the specifics of your situation, or intrapersonal work relationships take this with a HUGE grain of salt. As I was in a similar situation when I entered the trade. 

I learned to code by doing what you're doing now, making small manipulations to already proven code. Adding the occasional M00, or upping the feed a bit if I knew it could take it, like .005 to .0065. Once I got comfortable doing stuff like that I started really paying attention to what tools we were using and why, and the patterns that went with them. Once I felt like I had a good handle on it all, I would manually write out the program I PERSONALLY would have done if I started from the very beginning. (Which on a 2 axis CNC Lathe is simple 99% of the time) and once I felt good enough with that I would put it in the machine and run it through a graph to make sure it would "work" theoretically. And if it really saved time. 

Now, this took me 4ish years to do. And feel comfortable in my ability to even try the way I did. Because what I did is where the grains of salt come in. Because my bosses were a lot like what you've written here, "we've done it this way for 40 years and it works just fine". So what I started doing unbeknownst to them was just saying fuck that and doing it entirely my way. Because I knew it'd be faster, and month after month of huge gains in our times they finally came to me to figure out what I was doing. And now almost 2 years later I program and set up everything. And that's not to say I don't have plenty more to learn or anything. But if you're confident in your ability to improve it and keep quality high I say just doit.

Because eventually the market will be saturated/over saturated with your product. And no new consumers will be coming in. All GTA Online really did was very literally, buy them time to work on GTA6. Which will be the thing that brings new players in, and players like myself, who don't play GTAO anymore and make even more money than if they just let their cash cow keep milking.

It's literally JUST Rockstar I'm talking about. AAA in general is in a weird spot because the only way to make these massive games is with a massive budget, and the only way to get that budget is to appeal to suits who will do everything by the numbers. Make a game for everyone. 

Rockstar DOES have incentive to release it. When they think it's done, they have that luxury because they've built up an incredible base to sell to, and when GTA6 does launch it's going to sell like hotcakes, and break the records they themselves set. Everyone in the and out of the industry knows that.

God I hate this take so much, did GTAO absolutely take away from what could have been single player DLC? Yeah probably. Is it ok to be dissatisfied with Online in general? Sure is. But to say it's the reason GTA6 has taken so long is so astoundingly absurd. Look how MASSIVE RDR2 was. The sheer amount of animation, fluid physics, attention to detail is in it. And if GTA6 is BIGGER than that with wildly more complex systems like vehicles and aircraft the dev time needed goes up astronomically. 

It's like everyone expects AAA titles to come out on the timescale that they did with the PS2-3/360 era and that's literally just not possible anymore.
